threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver doesn’t say the stops; the locals just know to keep an eye out or check their phone.
Caught a guy on the 196 last night trying to sell his mixtape. He ended with a dramatic ‘next stop: fame!’ Classic Brixton vibe.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was really in Neukölln when I saw a spontaneous dance party break out in the subway station, complete with a saxophonist. Only here!

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that serves vegan döner, complete with homemade sauces and a terrace that feels like an oasis.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they can name the BART delays by heart, yet still shrug it off to grab a burrito at 11pm, while visitors panic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 47 with a guy wearing a full tuxedo and flip-flops. Muni's a stage and we're all just characters in this wild play.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's plazas are just for lounging, but locals actually use them for gatherings and spontaneous parties. It's a whole vibe!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by the way they refuse to learn the Catalan names on the metro maps—still staring at the screens like they're in a foreign country.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the Tube' instead of 'the Overground'—that and not knowing the secret bus routes marks you as a newcomer.
Caught the 133 last night, and a guy was arguing with a drunk pigeon over a sandwich. The bird won, flew off with half the bun. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I spotted a kid selling lemonade on the corner, right next to a street artist painting a mural. That vibe is pure Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, there’s an old tram line that’s basically a rolling art gallery - every car is painted differently. You can’t find that in other cities.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to avoid BART during Civic Center’s random evacuations. Tourists are still baffled by smoke alarms downtown.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 28 with a guy reciting Shakespeare to a half-asleep crowd. Only in San Francisco do you get free performances along with your ride.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí. But it's the little bakeries and independent shops on Carrer de Fr 33 that really capture our spirit.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their reluctance to order tapas; they always go for a full meal instead. Classic rookie mistake!
